body_html:
How to think about it

  • Capacity is how much a container holds: litres (L) and millilitres (mL).
  • Weight is how heavy something is: kilograms (kg) and grams (g).
  • Read the scale where the pointer stops.

Examples

Example

A jug holds 2 L. How many mL is that?

1 L = 1,000 mL

Answer: 2,000 mL

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Weighing a bag of rice in grams onlyHeavy things are measured in kg.
Reading the scale at the wrong markCount what each small mark is worth.

faq.q: What is the difference between capacity and weight?
faq.a: Capacity is how much a container holds; weight is how heavy something is.

faq.q: How many grams make a kilogram?

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much a rain barrel holds?
items.e: A rain barrel holds a lot of water, so use litres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, not capacity.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much a small bottle of vanilla holds?
items.e: A small bottle of vanilla holds only a little, so use millilitres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, not capacity.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a canoe?
items.e: A canoe is very heavy. It takes two people to carry it, so use kilograms. Millilitres and litres measure capacity, not mass.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a pencil?
items.e: A pencil is light. You could hold many pencils in one hand, so use grams. Millilitres and litres measure capacity, not mass.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much a teaspoon holds?

items.q: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth. 1,000 millilitres fill 1 litre: 1 L = 1,000 mL.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is heavier?
items.e: The left pan is lower. The lower pan holds the heavier object, so the pumpkin is heavier and the apple is lighter.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is heavier?
items.e: The right pan is lower. The lower pan holds the heavier object, so the bowling ball is heavier and the beach ball is lighter. A bigger object is not always heavier.

items.q: Rohan buys a bag of apples at the orchard. The scale shows its mass. He buys 2 more bags just like it. What is the mass of all 3 bags?
items.e: The scale shows 4 kg. 3 bags of 4 kg: 3 × 4 = 12 kg.

items.q: The water cooler at the Charity Run holds 18 L. Runners drink 9 L. How much water is left?
items.e: Water was used, so subtract: 18 − 9 = 9 L.

items.q: Ananya’s backpack has a mass of 7 kg. Her friend’s backpack has a mass of 5 kg. What is their total mass?
items.e: Put the masses together: 7 + 5 = 12 kg.

items.q: A bag of milk holds 4 L. A family drinks 1 bag each week. How much milk do they drink in 5 weeks?
items.e: 5 weeks of 4 L: 5 × 4 = 20 L.

items.q: A watering can holds 4 L. How many full cans are needed to give a garden 20 L of water?
items.e: How many 4 L cans make 20 L? 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cans.

items.q: A bag of sugar had 840 g. A baker uses 365 g for butter tarts. How much sugar is left?
items.e: Sugar was used, so subtract: 840 − 365 = 475 g.

items.q: On a canoe trip, each camper drinks 2 L of water a day. How much water do 4 campers drink in a day?
items.e: 4 equal groups of 2 L: 4 × 2 = 8 L.

items.q: A recipe needs 500 mL of milk. Priya has 350 mL. How much more milk does she need?
items.e: Find the missing part: 500 − 350 = 150 mL.

items.q: A box holds 5 bags of flour. Each bag has a mass of 2 kg. What is the mass of the flour?
items.e: 5 bags of 2 kg: 5 × 2 = 10 kg.

items.q: Dev fills a fish tank with a 5 L pail. He pours in 7 full pails. How much water is in the tank?
items.e: 7 pails of 5 L: 7 × 5 = 35 L.

items.q: A rain barrel had 33 L of water. A storm added 37 L. How much water is in the barrel now?
items.e: Add the water that came in: 33 + 37 = 70 L.

items.q: A puppy had a mass of 8 kg in the spring. Now it has a mass of 11 kg. How many kilograms did it gain?
items.e: Find the difference: 11 − 8 = 3 kg.

items.q: Kavya buys 9 bottles of water for a picnic. Each bottle holds 2 L. How many litres of water does she buy?
items.e: 9 bottles of 2 L: 9 × 2 = 18 L.

items.q: A fish tank has 28 L of water. Rohan adds 18 L more. How much water is in the tank now?
items.e: Adding more means add: 28 + 18 = 46 L.

items.q: Ananya has 48 kg of potatoes. She puts them into 6 sacks with the same mass. What is the mass of each sack?
items.e: Share 48 kg equally into 6 sacks: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 kg.

items.q: Om puts a book with a mass of 455 g and a pencil case with a mass of 185 g in his backpack. What is the total mass of the two things?
items.e: Put the masses together: 455 + 185 = 640 g.

items.q: One egg has a mass of about 50 g. What is the mass of 9 eggs?
items.e: 9 equal groups of 50 g: 9 × 50 = 450 g.

items.q: Yash picks 42 kg of apples. He packs them into 6 bags with the same mass. What is the mass of each bag?
items.e: Share equally: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 kg in each bag.

items.q: A bathtub had 137 L of water. Then 59 L drained out. How much water is left in the bathtub?
items.e: Water went out, so subtract: 137 − 59 = 78 L.

items.q: A bag of dog food has 18 kg of food. Siddharth's dog eats 3 kg each week. How many weeks will the bag last?
items.e: How many groups of 3 kg are in 18 kg? 18 ÷ 3 = 6 weeks.
